sections.label: Pallavi
sections.ta:
அணங்கொரு பாகம் கொண்ட அயவந்தநாதன்
இணையடி தொழுதிடத் துணை நானென்றிடத் துயரினியேது
sections.translit:
aNangoru bAgam koNda ayavandhanAthan
iNaiyadi thozhudhidath thuNai nAnendRidath thuyariniyEdhu
sections.en: The presiding deity of the Ayavandhi temple, Lord Ayavandhanadhan, has his consort as one half of his body. Will a devotee suffer after he has worshipped the Lord’s divine feet, and He has assured help?

sections.label: Anupallavi
sections.ta:
சேயிடைச் சிலம்பி கண்ட தாயெனத் தவித்தவள் திறங்காட்டி
துயிலிடை வந்தென்னைத் தூயவனாக்கி விட்டாய்
sections.translit:
sEyidaich chilambi kaNda thAyenath thavitthavaL thiRangkAtti
thuyilidai vandhennaith thUyavanAkki vittAy
sections.en: You came in my dream and showed me the greatness of my wife and purified my soul. You showed me the love she anxiously exhibited when a spider fell on your body. She was like a mother grieving, as though her baby was bitten by a spider.

sections.label: Charanam
sections.ta:
பரிந்தவளும் உன்திருமேனி தன்னில் ஊதி உமிழ்
சொரிந்த இடமெல்லாம் விடம் நீங்க ஏனைய புறம்
எரிந்த நிலை காட்டினாய் மனவிருள் நீங்கி ஒளி
தெரிந்த காலை சதி யாரென்றறிந்தேன் உமாபதியே
sections.translit:
parindhavaLum unthirumEni thannil Udhi umizh
sorindha idamellAm vidam nInga Enaiya puRam
erindha nilai kAttinAy manaviruL nIngi oLi
therindha kAlai sathi yArendRaRindhEn umApathiyE
sections.en: You showed me your body in a dream. Your entire body was burnt by spider venom except the areas that were covered by her saliva, which landed there when she blew the spider off your form. All my ignorance and darkness of mind vanished instantly. In this illuminated state, I realized my deeply pious wife’s devotion, Lord Umapathy.

notes:
This song was written for Smt. Indumathy Ganesh of Nrityollasa Dance Company, based in Fremont, CA. The song was set to music by Smt. Asha Ramesh in the ragam Hamsanandhi. This song was performed in a dance recital fundraiser for the SivaMurugan Temple in Concord, CA. The song is based on the life of the Saivite saint, Thiruneelanakkar. The song is written from the perspective of the saint, extolling Siva for clearing his mind and clarifying what devotion is. For more details on this episode, see:
பெரியபுராணம், 64 – வது நாயனார் தெய்வத்திரு திருமுருக கிருபானந்த வாரியார் சுவாமிகள், குகஶ்ரீ வாரியார் பதிப்பகம், 107 சிங்கண்ண தெரு, சிந்தாதிரிப்பேட்டை, சென்னை 600002, தொலைபேசி 8535 666, முதற் பதிப்பு: செப்டம்பர் 2000, பக்கம்: 398 – 406.
Per legend,Thiruneelanakkar was a devotee of Lord Siva in a town called Satthamangai. The temple was named Ayavandhi. Nayanar was devoted to Siva and, along with his wife, worshipped him daily at the temple. One day, when his wife was helping him with the prayers, she noticed a spider falling on the Sivalingam. She responded like a mother witnessing a venomous spider on her baby. She rushed to the idol and blew the spider away.
Thiruneelanakkar could not stand the desecration of saliva on his favorite Lord. He turned to his wife and told her that he was leaving her. He prayed again and returned home. His wife stayed in the temple all night, praying to the Lord to forgive her. Siva appeared in Thiruneelanakkar's dream and showed him his body. Siva explained that he had blisters everywhere in his body where the spider venom landed, except the places where the wife had spit. Neelanakkar realized the strength of his wife’s devotion and how Siva valued her reflexive response to the spider. He rushed to the temple, and prayed to the Lord with his wife on his side.
